Northwest Fisheries Science Center | NOAA Aquatic Invasive Gulf of Mexico Red Snapper Individual Fishing Quota Species Fact Sheet Invasive Lionfish NOAA recognizes that invasive species have a profound effect on aquatic ecosystems and is working to protect our coasts from these invaders. NOAA Invasi … ionfish invasion. NOAA is accomplishing its research missions on lionfish through strong collaborations with the Reef Environmental and Education Foundation (www.reef.org) and the United States Geological Survey (www.usgs.gov). Why are we concerned? In their native range, lionfish populations are controlled by predation, competition, and disease. In the Atlantic, Gulf of Mexico, and Caribbean they encounter few predators and are capable of reproduction year-round in warm waters. Lionfish are aggressive predators and have rapidly increased in number. Recent studies have documented significant impacts to native fish communities from lionfish predation.
